text:
ops-bot: ALERT: sudden p99 east-west latency spike in cluster-e during 11:05 batching ramp (SEV=critical)

noah: noticed p99 jump from ~5-7ms -> ~110-140ms across several GPU node pairs in rack-7 during the 11:05-11:10 window. A lot of batching traffic hitting NVLink-proxied RDMA paths.

samir: on it, pulling NIC counters, RDMA stats, and flow logs.

maya: can you check for MTU mismatches or jumbo/frame fragmentation? Also kernel offload flags (GRO/GSO/LRO) — previously that combo bit-rotted us.

noah: quick snapshot from node-e7: 
```
# ethtool -S mlx5_1 | egrep "tx_dropped|rx_errors|gso|lro"
tx_dropped: 4287
rx_errors: 94
large_receive_offload: on
generic-segmentation-offload: on
```

elena: infra-bot shows recent deploy on node-e9 updated NIC firmware last week — not all nodes are on same FW. RDMA pings at low QPS were fine earlier.

lia: this smells like host-side coalescing creating large frames that cross jumbo boundaries then force CPU-side reassembly under burst, causing RFIFO overflow and reorder.

samir: running iperf burst test across the rack to reproduce.

samir: ```
[  5]  0.00-10.00 sec  9.2 GBytes  7.9 Gbits/sec  16.3 ms  58 retransmits
```

maya: try disabling GRO on one victim and see if p99 improves for that pair. If it does, it's likely offload coalescing + FW/driver interaction.

noah: doing a controlled flip on node-e7 (draining one GPU slot first).

noah: `sudo ethtool -K mlx5_1 gro off gso off`

samir: after toggle, that node pair p99 dropped to ~20ms and tx_dropped fell by ~85%. Good signal.

elena: dmesg from node-e7 shows NIC FIFO events around the time of the ramp: 
```
mlx5_core 0000:3b:00.0: RFIFO overflow on PRIO 2
mlx5_core 0000:3b:00.0: FW error recovery triggered
```

lia: RFIFO overflow + FW recovery = transient path into slower handling, hence the 100ms tails during batching.

maya: immediate mitigation options:
- lower max_batch_size for rack-7 during 11:00-12:00
- enable per-pod rate limiting / inter-node smoothing
- consider disabling GRO/GSO as a short term node-level config for high-batch racks

noah: I've applied a temporary scheduler tweak: reduce max_batch_size by 35% for rack-7 peak window and added canary shift to rack-3 and rack-4.

elena: opened INFRA-2751 to track root cause and remediation (FW/driver parity sweep + host offload baseline). Assigned to samir and maya.

samir: next steps I'm taking: collect `ethtool -S` and RDMA counters from all rack-7 nodes, capture tcpdump/pcap of the bursts, and reproduce on a lab node with pktgen to confirm RFIFO triggers. I'll attach artifacts to INFRA-2751.

maya: also logging suggestion to evaluate NIC qdisc tuning (txqueuelen, fq_codel vs pie) and to consider defaulting GRO off for clusters serving large batched flows. Add to the ticket.

lia: note for post-incident: add a runnable playbook to detect mixed-FW racks and auto-quarantine or warn before heavy batching rollouts. Mixed firmware is a recurring vector here.

elena: temporary capacity policy created to route some large-model traffic away from rack-7 for the next 48h; monitoring alert thresholds lowered to warning while we observe.

noah: thanks team. Reopen thread if p99 spikes again — otherwise we'll treat as mitigated until the FW sweep completes. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: ALERT status -> warning (automated)
